product.audience: Climate, infrastructure and public-sector teams evaluating a dedicated orbital mission
product.decision: Understand platform deployment, coverage, payload capacity and mission pathway
product.conversion: Configure a mission profile and submit a technical concept request

signature.moment: A 3D spacecraft climbs from launch stack to orbit, unfolds its solar wings and paints an Earth coverage swath as the visitor advances mission events

systems.hero: A live orbital operations viewport sits beneath a compressed mission clock and systems rail, not a generic space photograph
systems.navigation: Mission elapsed-time rail with direct system anchors and concept-request status
systems.contentDensity: Operational telemetry and event data punctuated by a spatial Earth/spacecraft stage
systems.geometry: Orbital arcs, telemetry columns, coverage swaths, exploded satellite modules and mission event bars
systems.motion: Scroll or explicit event controls deploy the spacecraft and solar arrays; coverage animation advances only by scrub input, never autoplay
systems.coreInteraction: Visitors step launch, separation, deployment and imaging events, then configure orbit, payload and coverage into a mission concept

structuralDifferences: The first fold begins with current event, systems health and a square spacecraft viewport
Scroll choreography becomes four explicit event cards with previous and next mission controls
Coverage map becomes a vertical ground-pass strip
Mission configuration resolves as a compact concept uplink rather than a contact modal

artDirection.typography: Wide technical grotesk, monospace mission events and compact aerospace symbols
artDirection.material: Carbon-black bus, ceramic white structures, copper solar cells, ion-blue Earth limb and safety amber telemetry
artDirection.imageLogic: Spacecraft, Earth, solar arrays and coverage cone are code-native 3D; ground tracks and data views use SVG/CSS
artDirection.microcopy: MET, separation, AOS, downlink, revisit, swath, payload envelope, commissioning and concept review language
artDirection.dataHonesty: Mission performance, coverage and schedule figures are fictional illustrative estimates

assetStrategy: Two original cinematic mission frames complement the operational WebGL model: an orbital spacecraft campaign frame and a grounded mission-control proof frame, both local and explicitly fictional.

assets.role: Cinematic imaging-pass proof between deployment and coverage
assets.focalCrop: Spacecraft and Earth limb form a diagonal with room for telemetry
assets.mobileSafeArea: Spacecraft bus and blue atmospheric rim remain centered

assets.role: Human operational context for ground-network handoff
assets.focalCrop: Operator silhouettes, map light and consoles create depth without readable UI text
assets.mobileSafeArea: Central operator and blue console glow remain in frame

adjacentTemplates.why: Aviation rotates a route globe between airports; this stages spacecraft deployment, coverage and payload engineering over mission time.
A documentation spatial style is replaced by an operational mission event system and spacecraft deployment.
Orbital event telemetry and payload planning replace software workspace panels and generic AI utility.
Both are operational, but mission elapsed time and orbital coverage replace lap telemetry and strategy calls.
A spacecraft deployment sequence and ground network bear no structural relation to architectural camera itinerary and visit brief.
